fields.title: «Polka»: the budget that ran out mid-quarter
fields.summary: Error budget exhausted on day 18. Announced loyalty launch is in 12 days.
fields.decisionPrompt: What do we do in the remaining 12 days? State the cost of your decision.
fields.brief/role: You are a product manager at Polka.
fields.brief/company: Polka is a fictional grocery delivery service from local stores: 900 partner stores, a buyer app, and a partner portal.
fields.brief/context: You are a product manager at Polka. Checkout error budget is 43 minutes per month. On day 18 of the rolling window, 47 minutes were spent: three incidents in a row. By rule, new features are paused. In 12 days, the loyalty program launch is scheduled, date announced by marketing.
fields.brief/objective: Honor the intent of the error budget and avoid missing the announced date needlessly.
fields.brief/constraints: 12 days. Loyalty is half-ready and adds a link to the critical path.
fields.brief/task: Decide what you do in the remaining 12 days and what you tell marketing.
fields.learnTakeaway/title: Error budget manages the pace, it does not forbid work
fields.learnTakeaway/body: An exhausted budget means the next feature must not increase risk: preventable causes first, then release. This does not always mean 'stop everything' — sometimes it is enough to change the launch design so it does not lengthen the critical path. A rule broken at the first conflict stops working; a rule applied literally and indiscriminately stops being useful.
fields.evidenceCards/0/content: 21 minutes—retry storm during a brief network glitch. 17 minutes—database connection exhaustion after a release. 9 minutes—payment provider outage.
fields.evidenceCards/1/content: For the first—action «add jitter to retries», not done, owner on vacation. For the second—«configure gradual rollout», in progress. For the third—«expand Plan B», not started.
fields.evidenceCards/2/content: «Jitter to retries is 1 day. Gradual rollout is 3 days, half done. Plan B for payments already exists, expansion is 1 week. All three incidents were preventable».
fields.evidenceCards/3/content: Requires two weeks of work, half-ready. Affects checkout—points crediting is in the critical path.
fields.decisionOptions/0/label: Follow the rule: stop loyalty, fix reliability
fields.decisionOptions/0/description: Follow the rule: stop loyalty, fix reliability. 12 days for post-mortem actions.
fields.decisionOptions/0/consequence: rule works, three known causes are eliminated. Launch is postponed, announced date is missed. Second time following the rule in three quarters cements it.
fields.decisionOptions/1/description: Finish loyalty, reliability after launch. 12 days for loyalty.
fields.decisionOptions/1/consequence: date met. Rule broken for the second time out of three—effectively canceled. Points crediting adds a link to the critical path with an already exhausted budget.
fields.decisionOptions/2/label: Quick fixes plus loyalty with points crediting off the critical path
fields.decisionOptions/2/description: 4 days for jitter and gradual rollout, 8 days for loyalty with async points crediting.
fields.decisionOptions/2/consequence: two of three causes eliminated, launch happens, critical path is not lengthened. Expanding Plan B for payments postponed. Requires re-architecting the already finished half of loyalty.
fields.decisionOptions/3/label: Postpone launch by 10 days, do everything
fields.decisionOptions/3/description: Postpone launch by 10 days, do everything.
fields.decisionOptions/3/consequence: both reliability and loyalty fully done. Shift of announced date, but small. Marketing newsletter already sent.
fields.rubric/remediation/0/gap: Does not understand error budget as a pace management mechanism
fields.rubric/remediation/1/gap: Does not track completion of post-mortem actions
fields.rubric/remediation/2/gap: Does not see the connection between critical path length and availability
fields.rubric/remediation/3/gap: Retries and traffic spikes are not viewed as a source of self-inflicted failure
fields.rubric/remediation/4/gap: Error budget is not tied to release pacing decisions
